title: Remaking the Columbia string album with Danish strings
summary: Ann made him keep his old string scores, and a Danish record company records them again in stereo with the Danish symphony strings.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Including one called -- Sweet and Lovely which is sort of a remake of your Pretty Wild record, right?
Well, Ann had always said - I made

those two string albums for Columbia and, by some fluke I got the arrangement - not only got the arrangement but I got the scores as well and I carried them around from place to place with Ann, my wife and I kept saying to Ann - for God's sake - that heavy box -- let's get rid of that thing and she insisted we keep it. So, when I got to Denmark, I was talking to a big record company and I told them about this; they said, my God, why don't you get those arrangements - send them over here - and we'll make a record with the Danish strings. So, I did and I picked twelve songs from two record dates now - I mixed them up and I got the symphony strings of Denmark and all the fine musicians and we cut this thing and it was really, I think, much prettier and much better than the first ones I made for Columbia because now, of course, it was stereo; it was in stereo.
